relations.subject: vector-similarity-metric:euclidean-squared
relations.evidence: Use this method when you need higher performance than Euclidean Distance.

relations.subject: vector-similarity-metric:euclidean
relations.evidence: Only Hyperscale Vector and Composite Vector indexes support this metric. Search Vector Indexes do not support it.

relations.subject: vector-similarity-metric:euclidean-squared
relations.evidence: Only Hyperscale Vector and Composite Vector indexes support this metric. Search Vector Indexes do not support it.

relations.subject: vector-search:product-quantization
relations.evidence: Hyperscale Vector indexes and Composite Vector indexes support PQ quantization. Search Vector Indexes do not support it.

relations.subject: vector-search:flat-index
relations.evidence: Search Vector Indexes use a flat index when indexing datasets with 1000 or fewer vectors. Hyperscale Vector and Composite Vector indexes only support the next algorithm, IVF.

relations.subject: vector-search:scalar-quantization
relations.evidence: You do not choose a quantization method for Search Vector Indexes. Instead, they automatically choose whether to use quantization

relations.subject: index-type:hyperscale-vector
relations.evidence: Hyperscale Vector and Composite Vector indexes always use IVF as the basis of their indexes. In addition, they use a Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) graph to index the IVF's centroids.

relations.subject: vector-search:product-quantization
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - tradesOffAgainst. Reason: this content family (vector index quantization/algorithm choices) is dominated by explicit speed/accuracy/resource tradeoff statements that don't fit any promoted predicate; mustUseInsteadWhen implies a strict either/or substitution, but these are graduated cost/benefit tradeoffs.
relations.evidence: The process of quantization adds additional processing requirements to training. This overhead makes training a PQ index more computationally expensive than the other methods.

relations.subject: vector-search:scalar-quantization
relations.evidence: SQ has a lower training overhead compared to PQ because it does not search for clusters of vectors. Its training just determines the range of values for each dimension.

cross_component_finding: The four vector similarity metrics and two quantization methods described here are consistently gated by index TYPE (Hyperscale/Composite vs. Search Vector Index) rather than by version or edition, which is the dominant access-control axis for the rest of this batch's Capella content (Capella roles, credential-type privileges). This is a genuinely new gating axis - 'which index architecture supports this algorithm' - that doesn't map cleanly onto requiresPrivilege/requiresEdition/requiresCapellaRole; behavesDifferentlyUnder was the closest promoted-predicate fit but it's being stretched to mean 'is unsupported under' rather than just 'differs under'. Coordinator may want a dedicated supportsCapability/unsupportedUnder predicate for this recurring vector-index-family pattern.
